# Australian Bureau of Statistics (2025) — National, state and territory population, December 2024

**Source:** https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/population/national-state-and-territory-population/dec-2024.
**Venue:** ABS national resident population estimates, reference period December 2024, released June 19 2025.
**Read status (2026-10-17):** Original primary provider text or original publisher/university abstract as specified below.

## Contribution to the client commission

Primary ABS original release read. Year ended Dec 2024: net overseas migration +340,800, natural increase +105,200, national population growth +445,900. Their ratio ~76.43% of national population growth is migration, under separately rounded terms. These are all-resident components, not white-specific or Indigenous population classifications.

## Limits

National headcounts and rounded components may not sum perfectly; revision statuses apply. Do not equate temporary arrivals or net overseas migration with settler ethno-racial incorporation.

**Used by:** [Client publication commission dossier](../notes/2026/10/17/2026-10-17-client-publication-commission.md), comparative settler-society lane; not directly pooled with nineteenth-century slave-birth denominators.

## Commission-specific source audit (2026-10-17)

**Research role:** Australian component accounting, not white-cohort replacement.

**Evidence available at its source:** The Australian Bureau of Statistics' year ended 31 December 2024 estimates net overseas migration of about 340,800, natural increase of about 105,200, and total national growth about 445,900. The resulting migration share is approximately 76.4% of national **net growth**. Published rounded components can differ from an exact sum by approximately 100.

**Interpretive/measurement limits:** These numbers are about all usual residents and a particular year; they do not establish white racial classification or ethnicity of migrants. Contemporary migration dependence cannot be projected directly backward onto British colonial natural increase.

Evidence can be followed through the [23-claim crosswalk](bibliography-and-evidence-crosswalk-2026-10-17.md); the annotation is neither an assertion that every page of the source was read nor an independently replicated dataset.
